Learned counsel for the NHAI relies upon the ruling of this Court in National Highways Authority Of India vs Sheetal Jaidev Vade, 2022 SCC Online 1070, where the following directions were issued;
In view of the above discussion, we would have set aside the impugned judgment and order passed by the high Court on the aforesaid ground alone.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Sheetal Jaidev Vade, 2022 SCC Online 1070
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, taking into consideration the similar order passed by this Court in the case of Saraswatibai Chandrakant Shinde, we deem it appropriate to dispose of the present proceedings/appeal with the following directions;
1. The NHAI shall deposit 50% of the compensation amount, as awarded by the Arbitral Court, with the Executing Court within a period of four weeks.
The said amount shall be released to the land owners unconditionally.

2. The learned District Court, before whm the proceedings under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act are pending, shall make an endeavor to decide such proceedings within a period of six months from the next date of hearing before the said court.

3. The balance amount of compensation as per the Award to be passed under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act, shall be deposited by the NHAI with the Executing Court within four weeks, after such determination.
The said amount shall also be released by the Executing Court in favour of the land owners subject to the rights and remedies available to the parties in law.
4. Having considered the submissions and the judgment in Sheetal Jaidev Vade (Supra) we are of the opinion that an identical approach needs to be adopted.
It is submitted that the NHAI has deposited the entire amount including the enhancement directed by the arbitrator with the jurisdictional District Magistrate.

The said Magistrate is directed to release 50% of the said amount,
unconditionally to the land owners.
5. The District Judge, Barabanki is hereby directed to decide the applications under Section 34 pending before the Court within six months from today.
6. The special leave petitions are disposed of in the above terms.
7. Pending applications, if any, are disposed of.
Learned counsel seeks liberty to withdraw the petition.
Liberty sought for is granted.

opennyai_summary.facts:
In these proceeding National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) acquired notified lands for acquisitions.
The lands were assessed to compensation by the concerned competent authority.
. Aggrieved, the land owners approached the arbitrator, which enhanced the amount to 32.52 per sq. ft. with 9% interest in SLP(C) No. 11327/2019 and 52 per sq. ft. in SLP(C) No. 17322/2019, SLP(C) No. 17161/2019.
The NHAI was aggrieved and challenged this award under Section 34, Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
During the pendancy of those proceedings certain rules were amended, as a result of which, no portion of the enhanced amount could be released to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.decision:
However, taking into consideration the similar order passed by this Court in the case of Saraswatibai Chandrakant Shinde, we deem it appropriate to dispose of the present proceedings/appeal with the following directions;
1. The NHAI shall deposit 50% of the compensation amount, as awarded by the Arbitral Court, with the Executing Court within a period of four weeks.
The said amount shall be released to the land owners unconditionally.
2. The learned District Court, before whm the proceedings under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act are pending, shall make an endeavor to decide such proceedings within a period of six months from the next date of hearing before the said court.
3. The balance amount of compensation as per the Award to be passed under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act, shall be deposited by the NHAI with the Executing Court within four weeks, after such determination.
The said amount shall also be released by the Executing Court in favour of the land owners subject to the rights and remedies available to the parties in law.
4. Having considered the submissions and the judgment in Sheetal Jaidev Vade (Supra) we are of the opinion that an identical approach needs to be adopted.
It is submitted that the NHAI has deposited the entire amount including the enhancement directed by the arbitrator with the jurisdictional District Magistrate.
The said Magistrate is directed to release 50% of the said amount,
unconditionally to the land owners.
5. The District Judge, Barabanki is hereby directed to decide the applications under Section 34 pending before the Court within six months from today.
6. The special leave petitions are disposed of in the above terms.
7. Pending applications, if any, are disposed of.
Learned counsel seeks liberty to withdraw the petition.
Liberty sought for is granted.
The special leave petition is dismissed as withdrawn.
Pending applications, if any, are disposed of.
